scope: The private original-instance finalizer runs after test hooks, fixture teardown and failed-worker cleanup. It validates and disables only the separate pinned export timeout slot, leaving original test outcomes and the default timeout unchanged.
All five journal appenders stop before sealing. Public final-attachment steps remain visible to reporters without reentering their own sealed journal. Repeated installation and stop are idempotent.

Abandoned attempts dispose without reading final file/source resources. Retained journals use a 30-second preparation deadline with monotonic rechecks. Once atomic rename starts, the finalizer awaits its definitive success or failure.

Two-second foreground cleanup grace does not release original work, directory, file or archive ownership. Delayed preparation and cleanup retain their original owner; a late archive cannot enter a successor or export after cancellation.

Trace and screenshot diagnostics accumulate bounded messages and publish a completed attachment body once after foreground cleanup. Trace errors inspect only data messages; screenshots preserve their established original stack format and fall back to the safe message if formatting throws.

Actual pinned-runner and packed-consumer cases preserve passed and expected-failed outcomes through capture failure, cleanup failure, healthy successors and final preparation longer than the project export slot. Successful ZIPs stay attached when cleanup later fails. Screenshot reporter text and its original trace resource match exactly.

retainedFinding.finding: Pinned onAttach serializes body bytes immediately when an attachment is pushed. The initial finalizer and existing screenshot recorder pushed an empty body before updating its summary, leaving empty reporter diagnostics. Shared bounded accumulation now publishes completed bytes once after foreground cleanup; controlled insertion snapshots and actual reporter/trace comparisons prevent recurrence.
